Sanam Patel: quick question for the API docs + router impl — how do we want to define precedence between `model_pin`, `model_hint`, `region_hint`, `tier_hint` and a new `allowed_fallbacks` array? I added an example to the PR but want to make sure the behavior is correct before the rollout.

Sanam Patel: example request I used for testing:
```json
POST /v1/choices
{
  \"model_pin\": \"redwood-13b-q4\",
  \"model_hint\": [\"redwood-16b\", \"gptx-lite\"],
  \"region_hint\": \"us-west-2\",
  \"tier_hint\": \"balanced\",
  \"allowed_fallbacks\": [\"redwood-7b-q3\"]
}
```

Kevin Zhou: short answer: `model_pin` wins if available/capable. If `model_pin` is not deployable for the request (capacity, incompat, region), we consult `allowed_fallbacks` first, then `model_hint` list order, then global routing heuristics that consider `region_hint`/`tier_hint`.

Kevin Zhou: important nuance — `allowed_fallbacks` is explicit opt-in: it narrows what we are allowed to pick as fallback. If empty or missing, normal hints + default fallback list used.

Maria Gomez: what does the client see in the response when fallback happens? do we expose both the requested and served model fields?

Sanam Patel: good point. PR proposes response fields: `served_model`, `served_variant`, `request_model` (echo of `model_pin` or top of `model_hint`) and `fallback_used`: true/false. Example response we currently emit:
```json
200 OK
{
  \"id\": \"r_123\",
  \"request_model\": \"redwood-13b-q4\",
  \"served_model\": \"redwood-7b-q3\",
  \"served_variant\": \"quantized-v2\",
  \"fallback_used\": true
}
```

Tyler Nguyen: backward compatibility check — if a client sends unknown fields (eg `allowed_fallbacks` older client), server should ignore unknown fields and proceed. If an older client doesn't provide `allowed_fallbacks`, behavior is unchanged. We need to document that `allowed_fallbacks` is optional opt-in.

Kevin Zhou: also callout: if `model_pin` is incompatible due to seq-len / kv cache mismatch with the tokenization/format, we treat it as "unavailable" and then fallthrough; we should surface `unavailable_reason` in debug logs only (not users).

infra-bot: routing-policy-check: `model_pin` precedence asserted. Fallback candidates filtered by compatibility rules -> `allowed_fallbacks` applied -> hint ordering -> region/tier heuristics.

Maria Gomez: can we add a microtest that asserts when `model_pin` is down in us-west-2, an `allowed_fallbacks` list containing only a eu model does NOT get selected unless region override is allowed? We should prevent cross-region auto-fallback unless `region_hint` explicitly allows it.

Kevin Zhou: agreed. Policy: cross-region fallback requires either `region_hint` matching fallback region or `allow_cross_region_fallbacks=true` flag (we haven't added that flag; for now require explicit `region_hint`). I'll add a unit test and a routing integration test.

Sanam Patel: created PR #4321 with docs + router changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4321 — added docs for `allowed_fallbacks`, response fields, and a small state machine for checking compatibility. PTAL.

Kevin Zhou: I'll review this afternoon, pinging @Kevin for code review.

Tyler Nguyen: tiny nit — in the response sample please rename `request_model` -> `requested_model` for clarity.

Sanam Patel: done in PR. Thanks.

Maria Gomez: also add a short note in console UI that `fallback_used` may be true and link to served model details. Ops wants visibility.

Kevin Zhou: will add console note in a follow-up. Also adding a lint that flags `allowed_fallbacks` when it contains models not in our catalog.

Sanam Patel: cool. action items: 1) Kevin review PR #4321 (EOD) 2) Kevin add unit/integration tests for cross-region behavior 3) Maria add console note (follow-up) 4) Tyler confirm backward-compat doc snippet.

Sanam Patel: tagging this thread as the canonical async decision for precedence — will merge once Kevin lands review. :thumbsup:
